characters.description: A hobbit of the Shire, Bilbo's younger cousin and heir, who inherits Bag End and Bilbo's old ring when the old hobbit departs. Thoughtful and decent, he loves the Shire's quiet life but comes to shoulder a burden that will carry him far from home.
characters.name: Frodo Baggins

characters.description: Frodo's gardener and steadfast friend, a plain, loyal hobbit with a love of old tales and elves. Caught listening at the window while Gandalf reveals the ring's danger, he is enlisted as Frodo's companion and simply refuses to be parted from his master.
characters.name: Samwise Gamgee

characters.description: The wandering wizard, an old friend of Bilbo's, whose fireworks delight the Shire. Long uneasy about Bilbo's ring, he investigates its history and returns with grim news, setting Frodo on the road and guiding the growing effort against the rising Enemy.
characters.name: Gandalf

characters.description: Now very old but strangely unwearied, the hero of an earlier adventure. At his birthday party he vanishes using his ring and leaves the Shire for good, passing Bag End and - reluctantly, at Gandalf's urging - the ring itself on to Frodo.
characters.name: Bilbo Baggins

characters.description: A weather-worn Ranger first met at the inn in Bree, where he goes by Strider. Grim and watchful, he proves a friend and guides the hobbits toward Rivendell; he is far more than the rough wanderer he seems, being the long-hidden heir of ancient kings.
characters.name: Aragorn

characters.description: A capable, practical young hobbit and Frodo's cousin, one of the friends who has quietly guessed Frodo's secret and insists on sharing the journey rather than being left safely behind.
characters.name: Meriadoc Brandybuck

characters.description: Frodo's young, cheerful cousin, quick of tongue and eager for the road, who sets out with Frodo and Sam when they leave the Shire and becomes one of the company of travellers.
characters.name: Peregrin Took

characters.description: A proud, valiant warrior from the southern land of Gondor who comes to the Council of Elrond seeking help against the Enemy. Brave and well-meaning, he joins the company but is increasingly troubled by the thought of using the ring's power to defend his people.
characters.name: Boromir

characters.description: The ancient, wise, and beautiful elven Lady who rules the golden wood of Lothlórien and shelters the weary company. She tests each of them, gives them gifts for the road, and shows Frodo a glimpse of things that may come to pass in her mirror.
characters.name: Galadriel

characters.description: The unseen Dark Lord who forged the One Ring long ago to master all the others, and who now bends his will to recovering it. Though he never appears in person, his shadow spreads out of the land of Mordor and his servants hunt the ring across the world.
characters.name: Sauron

recaps.ending: Fellowship ends with the company broken at the falls of the great river Anduin. Boromir, overmastered by the ring's lure, tries to take it from Frodo; shaken, Frodo decides he must carry it to Mordor by himself rather than risk corrupting or endangering his friends. He slips away by boat, but Sam refuses to be left and forces his way aboard, so the two go east toward the Enemy's land together and alone. The rest of the Fellowship is left scattered and searching, unaware which way Frodo has gone. Gandalf is believed dead, lost in the deeps of Moria after his fall with the demon of fire. Aragorn, Legolas, and Gimli remain on the western shore, while Boromir, Merry, and Pippin are elsewhere along the river, their fates unresolved as the book closes. The ring is still whole and still far from the fire; Sauron's power grows and his armies stir, but the Enemy does not yet know exactly where the ring is. The quest is now split into two strands, two hobbits creeping toward Mordor and the sundered remnant of the Fellowship left to face the coming war, both carried forward into the next book.
recaps.in_short: The hobbit Frodo Baggins inherits a magic ring from his cousin Bilbo, and the wizard Gandalf reveals it to be the One Ring of the Dark Lord Sauron, who is rising again and hunting for it. To keep it from the Enemy, Frodo leaves the Shire with his friends Sam, Merry, and Pippin, pursued by Sauron's Black Riders. After narrow escapes and a near-fatal wound at Weathertop, they reach Rivendell, where a council decides the ring must be destroyed in the fire of Mordor where it was made. Frodo volunteers, and a Fellowship of nine sets out to help him: Gandalf, the ranger Aragorn, Boromir of Gondor, the elf Legolas, the dwarf Gimli, and the four hobbits. Blocked by mountains, they pass through the mines of Moria, where Gandalf falls battling a demon of fire. Sheltered and counselled by the elf-lady Galadriel, they travel on by river. At the last, Boromir tries to seize the ring, and Frodo, fearing its power over his friends, resolves to go on alone; only Sam manages to follow him as the Fellowship breaks apart.

recaps.text: Years ago the hobbit Bilbo Baggins, on an adventure with dwarves and the wizard Gandalf, found a plain gold ring deep under the Misty Mountains and took it from the creature Gollum. It made its wearer invisible, and Bilbo kept it quietly for the rest of his long life, using it now and then and telling no one its worth. What neither he nor anyone in the Shire knew was that this was the One Ring, forged in secret ages past by the Dark Lord Sauron to control all the other Rings of Power and to dominate Middle-earth. The Ring was cut from Sauron's hand in an ancient war and lost for centuries, passing at last to Gollum and then, by chance, to Bilbo. Now, after long years of hiding and slow recovery, Sauron has taken shape again in the land of Mordor and is searching everywhere for his lost Ring, whose return would make him unstoppable. His hunt is beginning to reach toward the quiet corner of the world where the Ring has lain forgotten.

At his eleventy-first birthday party in the Shire, Bilbo Baggins slips the ring on before the astonished guests, vanishes, and leaves the district for good, bequeathing Bag End and the ring to his young cousin and heir, Frodo. The wizard Gandalf, uneasy about the ring, presses Bilbo to give it up before he goes, and Bilbo does so with difficulty. Years pass. Gandalf's growing fears drive him to research the ring's history, and he returns to warn Frodo of the truth: the plain little ring is the One Ring of the Dark Lord Sauron, who is rising again and searching for it. Gandalf tells how the creature Gollum, who once owned it, has been captured and questioned, and has spoken of the Shire and of the name Baggins, so the Enemy now knows where to look. The ring cannot stay in the Shire. Gandalf sets Frodo to leave secretly, making for the elf-haven of Rivendell, and Frodo prepares to slip away with his gardener Sam, who is caught eavesdropping and enlisted as a companion.

Frodo sells Bag End as a cover and sets out on foot with Sam and his cousin Pippin, aiming for Rivendell. Almost at once a black-cloaked rider sniffs after them along the road, one of the Enemy's servants. They dodge the pursuit with help from passing elves and from Farmer Maggot, and reach the edge of the Shire, where Frodo's friend Merry reveals that he and the others already know about the ring and mean to come too. To avoid the watched roads the hobbits cut through the Old Forest, where a malevolent old tree nearly swallows them until a strange, powerful being named Tom Bombadil rescues and shelters them. Leaving his house, they are trapped by a barrow-wight among the ancient grave-mounds; Bombadil frees them again, and from the barrow-hoard they take old daggers well suited to hobbit hands. Gandalf, meanwhile, has failed to meet them as promised, and the hobbits press on toward the village of Bree, uneasy and still hunted.

At the inn in Bree the hobbits use the name Underhill, but Frodo draws attention when he accidentally slips the ring on and vanishes before a crowd. A weathered Ranger called Strider warns them they are in danger and offers to guide them; a letter left by Gandalf confirms he can be trusted and reveals that Strider is really Aragorn. That night the Black Riders attack the hobbits' abandoned room, and the party flees Bree with Aragorn into the wild. At the hill of Weathertop the Riders assail them, and their leader stabs Frodo in the shoulder with a cursed blade before Aragorn drives them off with fire. Frodo sickens as a splinter works toward his heart. Aragorn hurries them onward, and near Rivendell they are met by an elf who sets Frodo on a swift horse. At the ford of the river the Riders close in, but a sudden flood, raised by the elves' power, sweeps them away as Frodo, barely conscious, is carried across to safety.

Frodo wakes in Rivendell, healed by Elrond of the wound that would have made him a wraith, and is joyfully reunited with Sam, his cousins, the aged Bilbo, and Gandalf, who explains that he was delayed by the treachery of a fellow wizard, Saruman. Elrond calls a great council, where the ring's long history is laid out and the danger of Sauron's return is weighed. Every alternative is rejected: the ring cannot be wielded for good without corrupting its bearer, cannot be hidden forever, and cannot be given to the sea or the elves. The only course is to unmake it in the fire where it was forged, deep in Sauron's own land of Mordor. Frodo, though it terrifies him, offers to carry the ring. A Fellowship of nine is chosen to go with him: Gandalf; Aragorn and Boromir, a lord of Gondor; the elf Legolas; the dwarf Gimli; and Frodo's three hobbit companions, Sam, Merry, and Pippin.

The Fellowship travels south in secret. Turned back by a savage snowstorm on the mountain pass of Caradhras, which some suspect is the work of an enemy, they take instead the long dark road beneath the mountains through the abandoned dwarf-realm of Moria. At its western gate a many-armed creature in a black pool nearly seizes Frodo before they get inside. Within the vast, silent halls they find the tomb of Balin and a record of how the dwarf-colony there was destroyed. Attacked by orcs and a cave-troll, they fight their way toward the eastern exit, but at the Bridge of Khazad-dum a Balrog, an ancient demon of fire and shadow, bars the way. Gandalf makes a stand on the narrow bridge and breaks it beneath the creature, but the Balrog's whip drags him down into the abyss as he falls, and he is lost. The grieving survivors escape into the daylight.

Leaderless and mourning Gandalf, the company comes to Lothlorien, a hidden elvish realm of great beauty and power ruled by the Lady Galadriel and Lord Celeborn. The elves shelter and heal them. Galadriel quietly tests the hearts of the Fellowship and, at their asking, shows Frodo and Sam visions in her mirror of things that were, are, and may yet come, including the Shire under threat. Frodo offers her the ring, but she refuses the temptation to take it and remains herself. Rested, the travellers are given boats, grey elvish cloaks that hide their wearers, waybread that sustains them on the road, and other parting gifts, among them a coil of rope for Sam and a phial holding a star's light for Frodo, to be a light in dark places. Gimli, at first wary of the elves, is won over and asks only for a strand of the Lady's hair. They set out down the great river Anduin, carried southward toward the borders of the enemy's country, the burden of the choice ahead growing heavier with every mile.

The Fellowship journeys down the Anduin, passing the towering carved kings that mark Gondor's ancient border, and lands to decide their course: onward to the fire of Mordor, or aside to the defence of Gondor's city, Minas Tirith. Boromir, who has come to believe the ring should be used as a weapon to save his people, follows Frodo apart and tries first to persuade and then to seize it. Frightened at how the ring can twist even a brave and honorable man, Frodo puts it on to escape him and resolves to go on to Mordor alone, rather than lead his friends to ruin or let the ring corrupt them. He means to slip away by boat unseen, but Sam guesses his plan, wades after him, and refuses to be left behind. The two cross the river together and set off eastward alone, while the rest of the company, searching for Frodo, is scattered, and the book ends with the Fellowship broken.

characters.description: Commander of the Ankh-Morpork City Watch and Duke of Ankh, a blunt, working-class copper who dislikes his own title and distrusts diplomacy. Lord Vetinari sends him abroad as an ambassador to the distant, dangerous country of Uberwald, a role he is spectacularly unsuited for and which he treats, at heart, as police work.
characters.name: Sam Vimes

characters.description: Vimes's wife, a large, warm, immensely capable aristocrat and famous breeder of swamp dragons. Well-connected and unflappable, she accompanies Vimes on his diplomatic mission and handles the social side of it far more gracefully than he does.
characters.name: Sybil Vimes

characters.description: A very tall man raised by dwarfs and a captain of the City Watch, honest and literal-minded, with a natural gift for leadership. He is romantically attached to the werewolf Angua.
characters.name: Carrot Ironfoundersson

characters.description: A sergeant of the City Watch and a werewolf, originally from an aristocratic werewolf family in Uberwald that she left behind. Capable and self-controlled, she is uneasy about the prospect of her homeland and her relatives re-entering her life.
characters.name: Angua von Uberwald

characters.description: A dwarf member of the Watch who works on forensic detection and who, unusually for a dwarf, openly presents as female. Precise and clever, she travels with Vimes into dwarf country, where such openness is provocative.
characters.name: Cheery Littlebottom

characters.description: A stout, cautious sergeant of the Watch who is left in charge of policing Ankh-Morpork while his superiors are abroad, a responsibility that quickly reveals the limits of his leadership.
characters.name: Fred Colon

characters.description: A scruffy, opportunistic corporal of the Watch of dubious pedigree, who carries a document certifying that he is human. He remains behind in the city with the skeleton Watch.
characters.name: Nobby Nobbs

characters.description: A troll sergeant of the City Watch, hugely strong and slower-witted in the heat, who accompanies Vimes on the journey to Uberwald as bodyguard and muscle.
characters.name: Detritus

characters.description: A scruffy, disreputable Ankh-Morpork street dog who can talk, a fact he keeps quiet. Cynical and streetwise, he attaches himself to the story as it moves and offers unsolicited canine commentary.
characters.name: Gaspode

characters.description: The dwarf about to be crowned ruler of the dwarfs at a grand coronation in Uberwald, a moment of high political tension. The ceremony depends on an ancient dwarf artefact of deep symbolic importance.
characters.name: The Low King

characters.description: Angua's brother, a powerful and aggressive werewolf of the Uberwald aristocracy who leads his family's clan. Physically imposing and openly contemptuous of weakness, he treats hunting and dominance as sport.
characters.name: Wolfgang von Uberwald

characters.description: A servant of the traditional Uberwald type, an Igor: lisping, scarred, endlessly helpful, and a master of surgery and stitchwork. He is assigned to assist Vimes at the embassy.
characters.name: Igor

recaps.ending: Vimes exposes the plot behind the theft of the Scone of Stone: a faction of traditionalist dwarfs arranged the crime and a forged replacement to control the succession. The forger's work is revealed, and the Low King, Rhys Rhysson, is properly crowned, using the moment to make a startling public admission about the relic that defuses its power as a weapon. Wolfgang von Uberwald, having hunted Vimes across the frozen countryside, is defeated, ending the werewolf clan's bid for dominance. Angua and Carrot reconcile and return together to Ankh-Morpork and the Watch. Vimes, glad to be done with diplomacy, heads home, where the chaos Colon caused is quietly undone. Lady Sybil shares happy news with Vimes: she is expecting their first child. Ankh-Morpork's interests in Uberwald are secured, and Vimes returns to the job he actually wants.
recaps.in_short: Lord Vetinari sends Commander Vimes to the wild country of Uberwald as Ankh-Morpork's ambassador, ostensibly for the coronation of a new dwarf Low King but really to secure trade in the region's fat and mineral wealth. Vimes, his wife Lady Sybil, and a small party of watchmen arrive to find the dwarfs in crisis: the Scone of Stone, the ancient relic on which the Low King is crowned, has been stolen. Vimes treats the diplomatic emergency as a criminal investigation, tangling with scheming deep-down dwarfs, vampires, and the werewolf clan of Uberwald, led by Angua's violent brother Wolfgang. Angua returns home ahead of the others and Carrot resigns from the Watch to follow her. Back in Ankh-Morpork, the Watch nearly falls apart under Colon's mismanagement. Vimes uncovers that the theft is part of a plot to control who becomes Low King, survives a lethal hunt across the snow, and exposes the conspiracy in time for the true relic's fate to be revealed and the rightful coronation to proceed.

recaps.text: Previously, in earlier books: Sam Vimes rose from a broken-down captain to Commander of the Ankh-Morpork City Watch and, by marrying the aristocratic dragon-breeder Lady Sybil, became Duke of Ankh. He built the Watch into a large, mixed force of humans, dwarfs, trolls, and others, among them Captain Carrot, a human raised by dwarfs who is rumoured to have a claim to the city's vacant throne but prefers to stay a watchman, and Sergeant Angua, a werewolf who left her homeland behind. In a recent crisis, when a risen island nearly triggered a war between Ankh-Morpork and the empire of Klatch, Vimes refused to treat murder as patriotism and helped stop the conflict before it began. As this book opens, he is a reluctant fixture of the city's ruling class, still happiest working as a policeman.

Lord Vetinari appoints Commander Vimes, to his dismay, as Ankh-Morpork's ambassador to Uberwald, a remote and dangerous land of dwarfs, vampires, and werewolves. The official occasion is the coronation of a new dwarf Low King; the real business is trade and influence over the region's valuable resources. Vimes and Lady Sybil prepare to travel far from the city Vimes knows, into a place where he has no authority and few of the rules he relies on apply.

characters.description: A woman in her forties living quietly in the small southern comm of Tirimo, where she teaches at the creche. She is an orogene: she can sense and shape the movement of the earth, a power the Stillness fears and usually answers with a lynching, so she has hidden it for years from her neighbors and from her husband. She taught both her children in secret, and harshly, to hide what they inherited from her. The book opens on the day she comes home to find her three-year-old son beaten to death and her husband and daughter gone, and on the day a rift opens across the width of the continent and begins a Season that may not end in her lifetime.
characters.name: Essun

characters.description: Essun's three-year-old son, a talkative and unusually quick child who had already begun to show orogeny at home. His father kills him before the book opens, and Essun sits with his body for two days before she can make herself move.
characters.name: Uche

characters.description: Essun's husband, a stone-knapper in Tirimo who works flint and glass and is well liked in the comm. Until the day the book opens he was an affectionate father. On discovering that his younger child was an orogene, he beat the boy to death and left the comm with their daughter.
characters.name: Jija

characters.description: Essun's daughter, a watchful, self-possessed girl who inherited her mother's orogeny and was drilled in secret to keep it hidden and controlled. She is not in Tirimo when the book opens: her father has taken her south. Finding her alive is the reason Essun leaves home at all.
characters.name: Nassun

characters.description: A girl from a small northern village who is locked in her family's barn after her orogeny surfaces in front of the other children at school. Her parents have sent for someone to take her away. Proud, stubborn, and quick to reason her way through a bad situation, she understands that her family has given her up and is trying to work out what she is worth to anyone now. She is bright, she does not cry where people can see her, and she wants very badly to be kept.
characters.name: Damaya

characters.description: A Guardian, one of the order that finds orogene children and delivers them to the Fulcrum or kills them where they stand. He arrives to collect Damaya: an enormous man with long black hair, pale eyes, and an easy affectionate manner that never quite matches what he does. He is genuinely warm toward the frightened child in his care and also, calmly, brutal with her, and explains both as necessary. Guardians can shut off an orogene's power with a touch, which is why the Fulcrum's orogenes obey.
characters.name: Schaffa

characters.description: Tirimo's doctor, a serious young man who grew up in the comm, trained elsewhere, and came back to it. He is one of the few people who treats Essun as a person rather than a rumor once the town turns suspicious, and he makes it clear that what she is does not surprise him.
characters.name: Lerna

characters.description: A four-ring orogene of the Fulcrum, the imperial institution in the capital that trains, houses and rents out the orogenes it can catch. She is competent, sharp-tongued, and impatient for the rings that would bring her better work and more freedom. The assignment she is given instead is a humiliation: clear a silted harbor in a provincial coastal city, in the company of the Fulcrum's most senior orogene, and conceive a child by him on the way, because the Fulcrum breeds its orogenes as deliberately as it trains them.
characters.name: Syenite

characters.description: The Fulcrum's only ten-ring orogene, far more powerful than anyone Syenite has met and used by the institution as both a tool and a stud. He is theatrical, sardonic, and openly contemptuous of the rules and deference that structure Syenite's whole life, which makes him exhausting to travel with. He appears unstable and half broken, and he is nevertheless right about a great many things she was never allowed to learn.
characters.name: Alabaster

characters.description: A small boy Essun finds on the road south: naked, filthy, entirely unafraid, with white hair, white skin and eyes like clear ice. He gives his name as Hoa, will not say where he came from, and attaches himself to her journey on the claim that he can help her find her daughter. He does not eat ordinary food, is stronger and stranger than a child should be, and knows things about the roads, and about Essun, that he has no way of knowing.
characters.name: Hoa

characters.description: A filthy, foul-tempered commless traveler who takes up with Essun and Hoa on the road south and will not be shaken off. She is educated far past anything a road scavenger should be, obsessively interested in obelisks and in ancient ruins, evasive about where her learning came from, and unnervingly curious about Essun in particular.
characters.name: Tonkee

characters.description: A stone eater: one of the rare statue-like beings who move through solid rock as easily as a person walks through air, hold impossible stillness between one moment and the next, and take an interest in orogenes for reasons they decline to explain. She gives her name as Antimony, fixes her attention on Alabaster, and does not leave.
characters.name: Antimony

characters.description: A girl of a wealthy Leadership family in the capital who bribes and lies her way onto the Fulcrum's grounds while Damaya is training there. She is not an orogene. She is looking for something the city's oldest records say lies beneath the compound and that no one in authority will admit exists.
characters.name: Binof

characters.description: The leader of Meov, an island comm whose people live by raiding the ships that pass their stretch of coast. He is huge, loud and generous, and he is an orogene who was never taken by a Guardian and never trained by the Fulcrum, self-taught in ways the Fulcrum insists are impossible and unashamed of any of it.
characters.name: Innon

characters.description: The son born to Syenite and Alabaster on Meov: a calm, strong child raised beyond the Fulcrum's reach, and powerful from the moment he can reach for anything at all.
characters.name: Corundum

characters.description: The headwoman of Castrima, a comm built underground inside a geode. She is openly an orogene, recruits others instead of hiding them, and holds together a settlement in which orogenes and ordinary people share the same space, which nowhere else on the continent manages. Self-taught, dry, and relentlessly practical about what the arrangement costs.
characters.name: Ykka

recaps.ending:
Meov, the island comm where Syenite has lived free for two years, is found. A Guardian ship arrives, Schaffa among the boarding party, and Guardians can switch an orogene off by touch. Innon is killed in the fighting. Antimony takes Alabaster away through the rock. Cornered, and certain that Schaffa intends to carry her infant son off to a node station and wire him into a chair, Syenite kills Corundum herself, then reaches through a garnet obelisk and destroys Meov and everyone left on it. She survives, walks away from the wreck of her life, and starts again under another new name.

The three threads are one life. Damaya became Syenite; Syenite became Essun. The woman in Tirimo is the girl from the barn and the Fulcrum orogene, decades apart, renamed each time she had to begin again. The man who tore the continent open in the prologue is Alabaster.

In the present, Essun, Hoa and Tonkee reach Castrima, a comm hidden inside a geode underground and led openly by an orogene named Ykka. Alabaster is there: most of his body already turned to stone, the rest being consumed by Antimony. He admits that he opened the Rift deliberately, that the Seasons are an injury rather than a fact of nature, and that he needs Essun to finish what he began. His question closes the book: has she ever heard of a thing called a moon. Jija and Nassun are still alive somewhere to the south, and Essun has not stopped looking.
recaps.in_short: The Stillness is a continent whose civilizations are periodically ended by seismic catastrophe, and whose orogenes, people who can still or start earthquakes, are feared, owned and killed. Three stories run in parallel: Damaya, a girl handed to a Guardian and raised in the imperial Fulcrum; Syenite, a Fulcrum orogene sent on assignment with the powerful, insubordinate Alabaster and shown by him how much the empire hides; and Essun, a middle-aged woman in a small comm who comes home to find her small son murdered by her husband and her daughter taken, on the same day an orogene tears a rift across the continent and begins a Season expected to last centuries. Syenite's thread ends with a free comm destroyed by Guardians, her lover dead, and Syenite killing her own infant son rather than let him be enslaved. The three women are one: Damaya became Syenite, Syenite became Essun. Essun reaches the underground comm of Castrima and finds Alabaster there, dying and half turned to stone. He admits he broke the world on purpose, and asks whether she has ever heard of a thing called a moon.

recaps.text:
The Stillness is a single continent shaken so regularly that every institution on it is organized around survival: comms stockpile against Fifth Seasons, the long ash winters that end eras, and stonelore tells everyone how to live through one. Orogenes can sense and control the movement of the earth. They are hated and commonly killed on discovery; the empire of Sanze controls the ones it catches through the Fulcrum, an institution in the capital of Yumenes, and through the Guardians, who collect orogene children and can shut their power off with a touch.

The book opens with two endings. In Yumenes, a man of extraordinary power tears a rift across the width of the continent, destroying the capital and beginning a Season that will last centuries. In the small southern comm of Tirimo, a woman named Essun comes home to find her three-year-old son Uche beaten to death by her husband Jija, who has taken their daughter Nassun and gone. Essun is an orogene who has hidden it for years, and so were her children. When the shockwave from the north reaches Tirimo she instinctively turns it aside from the comm, and the town, which now suspects what she is, becomes dangerous to her. She buries her son and leaves through the gate, heading south after Jija and Nassun.

Elsewhere in the Stillness, a girl named Damaya is locked in her parents' barn after her orogeny surfaces at school. A Guardian named Schaffa comes for her and takes her away.

Essun travels south on the Imperial Road as ash begins to fall from the north and comms shut their gates against strangers. She is joined by a small boy who calls himself Hoa: white-haired, white-eyed, afraid of nothing on the road, who says he can help her find her daughter and will not say where he came from.

Schaffa takes Damaya north toward Yumenes. On the way he deliberately breaks her hand, then sets it and tends her, explaining that she has to learn she cannot hurt him and that he will hurt her whenever it is necessary. He also tells her what she is worth: an orogene is a tool that can save a comm or destroy one, and the Fulcrum exists to make the difference reliable. Damaya, discarded by her family, decides to become worth keeping.

In Yumenes, Syenite is a four-ring orogene of the Fulcrum, proud of her rank and impatient for more. She is handed an assignment she resents: travel to the coastal city of Allia and clear its silted harbor, in the company of Alabaster, the Fulcrum's only ten-ringer, and conceive a child by him on the way, because the Fulcrum breeds its orogenes as deliberately as it trains them. Alabaster proves to be powerful beyond anything she has seen, openly contemptuous of the rules she has built her life on, and apparently unstable.

Damaya arrives at the Fulcrum and is enrolled as a grit, the lowest rank, in a compound where orogene children are drilled in control, punished hard for failure, and reminded constantly that every one of them was given up by their family. Rings are earned by examination and mark rank. The Guardians are always present.

Syenite and Alabaster travel toward Allia. He is exhausting company, and he shows her things the Fulcrum never taught: that orogeny can be done with a precision she was told was impossible, and that the empire's remarkable seismic stability is paid for. At a node station along the road they find the maintainer, an orogene child mutilated and wired into a chair, kept alive to quell shakes automatically for the region around it. The station's attendant is missing and the maintainer is dead. Syenite understands that this is where the Fulcrum's failures go, and that any child of hers could end there.

Essun goes on south with Hoa through thickening ashfall, past comms that have already closed and settlements already emptied. She avoids the trouble she can and keeps moving toward the roads her husband is most likely to have taken.

Syenite and Alabaster reach Allia, a coastal city that resents needing them, and clear the blocked harbor. In the seabed Syenite finds something that should not be there: a broken obelisk, one of the enormous crystals that drift unexplained above the continent, sunken and buried, with the body of a stone eater inside it. Alabaster reacts with real fear and will not fully explain why. Their standing with Allia's leadership deteriorates from there.

At the Fulcrum, Damaya learns the institution's real curriculum: absolute control, absolute obedience to Guardians, and the understanding that an orogene's life is held on sufferance. She trains, makes a few careful friendships among the other grits, and works toward her first ring.

On the road, Essun and Hoa continue south. Hoa steers her toward routes she would not have chosen, is never hungry, and comes to no harm from things that should harm a child. She keeps him anyway, because he claims to be able to follow her daughter's trail and she has nothing better to follow.

Allia ends. Under attack and out of options, Syenite reaches for the drowned obelisk, and what answers is beyond anything she can hold. The city is destroyed and its harbor becomes a smoking crater. She and Alabaster survive, and a stone eater who gives her name as Antimony, and who has attached herself to Alabaster, carries them both through solid rock to Meov: an island comm in the northern sea whose people live by raiding and whose orogenes have never been near a Guardian.

At the Fulcrum, Damaya meets Binof, a girl of a Leadership family who has talked her way onto the grounds looking for something the city's oldest records say lies underneath them. The two of them find it: a vast buried chamber far older than Sanze, holding a socket the size and shape of an obelisk. They are caught, and the Fulcrum's reaction makes clear that the chamber is a secret worth keeping.

Essun's road south brings her a second companion, Tonkee: filthy, sharp, commless, far too educated for a scavenger, and openly fascinated by obelisks and by Essun herself.

Syenite and Alabaster stay on Meov. Its people take them in without ceremony, and Innon, Meov's leader, turns out to be an orogene who was never caught, never trained and never taught to be ashamed. He becomes lover to both of them. Syenite bears a son, Corundum, and for the first time lives as a person rather than a resource: no rings, no Guardians, no assignments, no one measuring her. Alabaster is calmer than she has ever seen him, and he tells her more of what he knows about obelisks, about what Guardians actually are, and about how much of stonelore is a lie. Syenite also understands that they are fugitives, and that the Fulcrum does not simply write off property.

Elsewhere, Damaya's competence at the Fulcrum hardens into ambition, and she begins to be trusted with real work.

Essun, Hoa and Tonkee travel on through the ash toward the far south, arguing most of the way, and Essun stops pretending to herself that Hoa is a child.

Meov is found. A Guardian ship arrives, Schaffa among the boarders, and Guardians can switch an orogene off by touch. Innon dies in the fighting. Antimony carries Alabaster away through the rock. Cornered, and certain that Schaffa means to take her infant son to a node station, Syenite kills Corundum with her own hands, then reaches through a garnet obelisk and destroys Meov and everyone on it. She survives, walks away, and starts over under a new name.

The three threads are one life. Damaya became Syenite; Syenite became Essun. The girl in the barn, the Fulcrum orogene and the schoolteacher in Tirimo are one woman at three ages, renamed each time she had to begin again. The man who broke the continent in the prologue is Alabaster, who did it deliberately.

In the present, Essun, Hoa and Tonkee reach Castrima, a comm built inside a geode underground and led openly by an orogene named Ykka, where orogenes and ordinary people live in the same space. Alabaster is there, most of his body already turned to stone and the rest being consumed by Antimony. He tells Essun that the Seasons are the consequence of an ancient injury rather than a fact of nature, that they can be ended, and that he needs her to finish it. His last question to her is whether she has ever heard of a thing called a moon. Tonkee proves to be Binof, still chasing the answers she went looking for as a girl, and Jija and Nassun are still alive somewhere to the south.

characters.description: A half-skaa street thief in Luthadel, capital of the Final Empire, small and underfed and about sixteen years old. She survives inside a criminal crew by making herself useful and invisible, and by trusting no one, a lesson her older brother beat into her before he disappeared. She believes she possesses a knack she calls Luck, a faint influence that makes people better disposed toward her and keeps her crewleader from discarding her. She has spent her life under falling ash, hiding from the obligators of the Steel Ministry and from the nobility who own the skaa, and she has no expectation that anything about the world can change.
characters.name: Vin

characters.description: A half-skaa crewleader, charming, theatrical, and famous in Luthadel's underworld. He was sent to the Pits of Hathsin, the Lord Ruler's prison mine, where the labor kills everyone sent there, and he came back alive, the only person ever to do so. He returns to the city changed: he is now a Mistborn, able to burn every Allomantic metal, and he wants far more than the wealthy scores that made his name. His wife Mare died in the Pits, and behind the grin he carries an unbending hatred of the nobility and of the empire that made them.
characters.name: Kelsier

characters.description: Kelsier's oldest partner and the crew's organizer. He handles money, supplies, forged papers, and the hundred practical arrangements that keep an operation running while Kelsier makes speeches. He is not an Allomancer and is quietly impatient with those who assume that makes him less useful. Steady and methodical, he is the crew member most likely to say plainly that a plan is madness, and then set about arranging it anyway.
characters.name: Dockson

characters.description: The brutal thieving crewleader Vin works under, a heavy, self-important man who beats those beneath him and is running an elaborate fraud on the Ministry's canal contracts. He keeps Vin close because her presence makes negotiations go his way, though he does not understand why, and he is quick to remind her that she survives only at his pleasure.
characters.name: Camon

characters.description: Vin's older brother, who raised her after their mother was lost and who taught her to survive by expecting betrayal from everyone, including him. He hurt her deliberately so the lesson would hold, then vanished and left her with the crews. He is absent from her life when the book opens, but his voice still argues with her in her head whenever she is tempted to trust somebody.
characters.name: Reen

characters.description: The crew's Soother, an Allomancer who burns brass to dampen other people's emotions. Plump, impeccably dressed, and fond of a cane and a glass of wine, he treats manipulation as a craft and complains loudly about any work that requires him to walk. His arch, needling manner hides a genuinely formidable talent for steering a room.
characters.name: Breeze

characters.description: The crew's Thug, an Allomancer who burns pewter for strength and endurance, built like a soldier and cheerful about it. He enjoys picking at moral and logical puzzles and inflicting them on anyone who will argue back. He keeps his wife and children living away from him under a false name, because association with Kelsier's work would kill them.
characters.name: Ham

characters.description: The crew's Smoker, an Allomancer who burns copper to hide other Allomancers from detection. He is old, sour, and lame in one leg from imperial military service, and he runs a woodworking shop whose apprentices and workrooms give the crew a legitimate front and a base in Luthadel. He greets almost everything with a scowl.
characters.name: Clubs

characters.description: Clubs's nephew and the crew's Tineye, an Allomancer who burns tin to sharpen his senses and is used mainly as a scout and lookout. He is a teenager, eager to be taken seriously, and speaks in a clipped eastern street cant that most of the crew cannot follow.
characters.name: Spook

characters.description: The leader of the skaa rebellion, a stubborn, unglamorous man who has spent years keeping an underground movement alive in the slums. He hires the crew despite despising thieves on principle, and never stops saying so. He believes in the rebellion as a cause rather than as an operation, and distrusts Kelsier's showmanship.
characters.name: Yeden

characters.description: A Terrisman steward, tall, calm, and formally polite, assigned to teach Vin how to pass as a noblewoman. He is secretly a Keeper, a Feruchemist who stores knowledge in metalminds so that the histories, languages, and religions the Lord Ruler destroyed are not lost. He collects the beliefs of the dead peoples of the empire and offers them, gently and persistently, to anyone who might want one.
characters.name: Sazed

characters.description: Kelsier's older brother, severe and disapproving, who ran the skaa rebellion before Yeden and blames Kelsier for the disaster that ended with Kelsier in the Pits. He is a Seeker, an Allomancer who burns bronze to sense others using Allomancy. Grim and self-contained, he agrees to take on the most dangerous role in the crew's plan: joining the Steel Ministry as a spy.
characters.name: Marsh

characters.description: The heir of House Venture, one of the greatest noble houses of Luthadel. Young, untidy, and habitually late, he prefers to spend a ball hiding in an alcove with a book rather than dancing, which irritates his father and amuses almost nobody else. He reads banned political philosophy and has opinions about how the empire ought to be governed that he is careful to voice only among friends.
characters.name: Elend Venture

characters.description: The immortal emperor of the Final Empire, worshipped as God by his own priesthood and ruling from the palace of Kredik Shaw in Luthadel. He has held absolute power for a thousand years, having saved the world from a threat called the Deepness at the Well of Ascension, and he is remembered as having crushed every rebellion since. He is believed to be beyond killing, and the empire's whole order rests on that belief.
characters.name: The Lord Ruler

characters.description: The elite enforcers of the Steel Ministry, inhuman figures with heavy spikes driven point-first through their eye sockets and out the back of the skull, who nonetheless see perfectly well. They hunt skaa who show Allomantic ability, and they are strong, fast, and by reputation impossible to kill. Their attention is the thing every member of the crew most wants to avoid.
characters.name: Steel Inquisitors

characters.description: A noblewoman of House Elariel, poised and sharply intelligent, whose family expects her to marry Elend Venture and bind the two houses together. She takes an immediate interest in the unknown young woman from the provinces who has been occupying Elend's attention, and her courtesy at court carries an edge.
characters.name: Shan Elariel

recaps.ending: Kelsier provokes an open uprising in Luthadel, then confronts the Lord Ruler in the square before Kredik Shaw and is killed in front of the crowd. The death is deliberate: it turns him into the Survivor, a martyr whose legend pushes the skaa into a full revolt that the crew's shattered army could never have produced. Marsh, believed dead, is alive, having been made into a Steel Inquisitor, and uses that position to strike from within. Vin, having pieced together the Lord Ruler's own logbook with Sazed, understands that he is not the prophesied hero who saved the world but Rashek, the servant who murdered the true hero and took the power at the Well of Ascension for himself, and that his immortality is fed by great metal bracers driven through his arms. She fights him in the palace, tears the metal away, and he ages and dies. Luthadel falls to the rebellion. Elend Venture, the one nobleman who wanted a better arrangement, is made king of the city, with Vin beside him and the surviving crew members as his awkward, unqualified government. The atium hoard the crew came for is never found, the ash still falls, the mists still rise, and Kelsier is already being worshipped as a god by the people he freed.
recaps.in_short: Under the thousand-year rule of the immortal Lord Ruler, ash falls constantly, the skaa are owned as slaves by the nobility, and rebellion has never once succeeded. Kelsier, a half-skaa thief who survived the Lord Ruler's prison mine and came out of it a Mistborn, gathers a crew of Allomancers for an impossible job: overthrow the Final Empire. He recruits Vin, an abused street thief who does not know she is Mistborn too, and trains her while she infiltrates the nobility under a false name and falls in with Elend Venture, the bookish heir to a great house. The crew's secret skaa army is destroyed and the plan collapses, but Kelsier provokes Luthadel into revolt and lets the Lord Ruler kill him publicly, becoming a martyr. In the chaos Vin learns from the Lord Ruler's own journal that he is an impostor sustained by metal he wears, confronts him, and kills him. The empire's capital falls, Elend is made king, and the crew are left holding a city they never planned to govern.

recaps.text: The Final Empire has stood for a thousand years. Ash falls from the sky, mists rise every night, the skaa are property of the nobility, and the immortal Lord Ruler is worshipped as God by the priests of the Steel Ministry. Vin, a small, distrustful half-skaa thief, survives inside Camon's crew in Luthadel by using what she calls her Luck, an ability she cannot explain that makes people agreeable. Kelsier, a famous half-skaa crewleader, returns to the city after surviving the Pits of Hathsin, the prison mine that kills everyone sent to it, where his wife died and where he became a Mistborn, able to burn every Allomantic metal. He finds Vin, recognizes what she is doing, and takes her into his own crew. There he tells her the truth: she is Mistborn as well. He assembles his specialists, among them Dockson the organizer, Breeze the Soother, Ham the Thug, Clubs the Smoker, and young Spook, and reveals the job he wants them for. Hired by the rebellion leader Yeden, they intend to raise a secret skaa army, empty the Lord Ruler's legendary hoard of atium, and bring down the empire itself.

Vin begins training in Allomancy, learning to Push and Pull on metal to fly across the city, to burn pewter for strength and tin for sharpened senses, and to work the emotions of a room with brass and zinc. She struggles to accept that the crew treats her as one of their own rather than as something to be used. Kelsier assigns her a second role: posing as Valette Renoux, a young noblewoman newly arrived from the provinces, so she can move through the great houses and gather intelligence. The Terrisman steward Sazed is given charge of her education in manners, dress, and court politics, and privately reveals himself as a Keeper, a Feruchemist who stores the histories and religions the Lord Ruler erased. Kelsier's brother Marsh, who despises him, agrees to infiltrate the Steel Ministry as a spy, while a skaa army is quietly recruited and hidden in caves outside the city. Kelsier also begins a second campaign entirely his own: killing nobles at night so that the skaa will start to believe the empire can bleed.

Vin enters noble society and finds she is unexpectedly good at it. At a ball in Keep Venture she meets Elend Venture, heir to one of the most powerful houses, who spends parties in an alcove reading banned political philosophy and talks to her as if she were a person rather than a match. She keeps returning to the balls, telling herself it is for the crew's intelligence, and reports on house alliances and rivalries while the crew works to set the great houses against one another. At the same time Kelsier's night raids and public defiance are hardening into legend among the skaa, who are beginning to speak of the Survivor of Hathsin as something more than a thief. Dockson and Ham worry that Kelsier is enjoying the myth too much, and that he is keeping parts of the plan to himself. Vin, living two lives, finds both of them increasingly hard to put down.

The crew's work proceeds on several fronts. The hidden army drills in the caves under Yeden's nominal command, growing faster than anyone expected. Marsh sends word from inside the Steel Ministry, where he has been accepted as a prelan and is reading its records. Sazed and Vin study a stolen logbook written by the Lord Ruler himself in the days before he took the power at the Well of Ascension, an account that does not match anything the Ministry teaches: it speaks of a man travelling north to save the world from a threat called the Deepness, and of the Terris packman who guided him. Vin, meanwhile, is noticed at court by Shan Elariel, the noblewoman expected to marry Elend, and finds her position as Valette increasingly exposed. Out in the mists at night, Vin becomes convinced that something is following her, a shape in the fog that no one else will admit to seeing, and Kelsier dismisses it.

The crew's campaign against the great houses works better than anyone hoped. Assassinations, thefts, and forged evidence set the noble families against one another until Luthadel slides into open house war, with private armies fighting in the streets and whole houses fleeing the city, drawing the imperial garrison's attention away from the skaa. Kelsier's night killings continue, and the Survivor of Hathsin has become a figure the slums genuinely believe in, to the visible discomfort of a crew who know exactly how deliberately the legend was built. Elend, quarrelling with his father over how House Venture should respond, is increasingly exposed at court for his association with a provincial girl nobody can verify. The hidden army in the caves reports itself ready. Vin, still convinced something walks with her in the mists, is told by Kelsier to stop worrying about it and prepare for the part of the plan he has not yet fully explained.

The plan comes apart. The skaa army, impatient and badly led, moves against an imperial garrison without orders and is destroyed; most of the recruits are killed and Yeden dies with them. The crew is left with a fraction of the force the operation required and no way to rebuild it in time. Kelsier, blamed by his own people for building a myth instead of an army, refuses to abandon the job and begins improvising a different one, telling almost no one what it is. Vin's noble identity becomes untenable: Shan Elariel moves against her directly, Vin is forced to kill her, and Valette Renoux is finished as a cover. Elend, warned that association with her is dangerous, defends her anyway and is disowned for it by his father. Then word arrives from the Ministry that Marsh has been taken and killed, and the crew, already gutted, has lost its eyes inside the enemy.

Refusing to believe Marsh is dead, Vin breaks into the Ministry's own building to find him and is captured by Steel Inquisitors, who beat her nearly to death and use her to draw the crew out. The rescue costs them: Sazed spends his Feruchemical stores to reach her, and Kelsier faces an Inquisitor in single combat and kills it, the first time in a thousand years anyone has managed it. The victory is small against what they have lost. With the army gone, the treasury plan dead, and the crew hunted, Kelsier finally states his real intention, which does not depend on soldiers at all. Vin, recovering, works through the Lord Ruler's logbook with Sazed and begins to see that the history the Ministry preaches is a lie built on top of another man's journey, and that whatever the Lord Ruler actually did at the Well of Ascension, he was not the person the prophecies described.

Kelsier turns Luthadel out into the streets, breaking the city garrison and setting a full skaa uprising in motion, then walks into the square before the palace and lets the Lord Ruler strike him down in front of the crowd. His death is the point: the Survivor becomes a martyr, and the revolt that follows is far larger than anything his army could have achieved. Marsh, alive and transformed into a Steel Inquisitor after his capture, turns that position against his masters. Vin, having finished the logbook, understands the truth at last. The Lord Ruler is Rashek, the Terris packman who murdered the man the prophecies named and seized the power at the Well of Ascension for himself, and his immortality runs through the great metal bracers driven into his arms. She fights him in Kredik Shaw, tears the metal from his body, and he ages and dies where he stands. Luthadel belongs to the skaa. Elend Venture is made king of the city, the surviving crew members become his reluctant government, and Kelsier is already being spoken of as a god. The atium hoard is never found, and the ash keeps falling.

characters.description: The Dragon Reborn and now the Car'a'carn, chief of chiefs to the Aiel, wielding the crystal sword Callandor and learning to channel from a bound Forsaken tutor. Hardening under the weight of his role and the taint on the male Power, he means to unite the world behind him whether it wills or not, and he grows warier and colder as enemies close in.
characters.name: Rand al'Thor

characters.description: Rand's luck-blessed friend, changed by his passage through an ancient doorway into a man carrying dead soldiers' memories of war, a black-hafted spear, and a medallion that turns aside the Power. Still desperate to escape battle and destiny, he keeps finding himself uncannily good at both.
characters.name: Mat Cauthon

characters.description: The innkeeper's daughter of Emond's Field, trained in dreamwalking by the Aiel Wise Ones and grown formidable in the world of dreams. Ambitious and increasingly self-possessed, she moves between Rand's camp and the affairs of the Aes Sedai who oppose Elaida.
characters.name: Egwene al'Vere

characters.description: The former Wisdom of Emond's Field, a channeler of great strength who can still reach the Power only through anger, and a gifted Healer and dreamwalker. Proud and stubborn, she is locked in a personal duel of wits with the Forsaken who once nearly killed her.
characters.name: Nynaeve al'Meara

characters.description: The Daughter-Heir of Andor, a strong channeler traveling in disguise with Nynaeve as the two make their way toward the gathering of rebel Aes Sedai. Poised and determined, she is torn between her claim to a throne, her Tower training, and her love for the Dragon Reborn.
characters.name: Elayne Trakand

characters.description: The Aes Sedai who found the Dragon Reborn and has steered his path since Emond's Field, now yielded to a lesser hand in his counsels as he grows harder to guide. Calm and secretive still, she carries private knowledge of what may lie ahead and keeps her own counsel about it.
characters.name: Moiraine

characters.description: Moiraine's Warder, a grim and unequaled swordsman and the uncrowned last king of a lost Borderland realm. Bound to Moiraine, he remains her guardian and her shadow, dangerous and unshakably loyal.
characters.name: Lan

characters.description: An Aiel Maiden of the Spear who has set aside the spear to train as a Wise One and a channeler. Prickly, proud, and fiercely bound by Aiel custom, she has been set to watch over Rand and finds that duty steadily more complicated by her own tangled feelings.
characters.name: Aviendha

characters.description: The white-haired gleeman and former royal bard, worldly, wry, and shrewd, traveling as protector and adviser to Nynaeve and Elayne on their dangerous road. He hides old griefs and old loyalties behind a performer's easy manner.
characters.name: Thom Merrilin

characters.description: A famed archer-heroine out of legend, plainspoken, brave, and unmatched with a bow, who becomes a close and unexpected companion to Nynaeve and Elayne. Loyal and matter-of-fact, she adapts warily to a strange new time and to friends she never expected to have.
characters.name: Birgitte

characters.description: One of the Forsaken, the Dark One's ancient champions freed from long imprisonment, called the Spider for her patient cruelty. Having already clashed with Nynaeve, she prefers traps, stealth, and manipulation from the shadows to open confrontation, and she nurses a grudge against the young women who defied her.
characters.name: Moghedien

recaps.ending: The book closes in loss and grim victory. At Cairhien, Moiraine confronts the Forsaken Lanfear, who has come in a jealous rage over Rand, and hurls them both through a twisted doorway that appears to destroy them both, leaving behind a letter of farewell and quiet final instructions. Rand is left grieving the Aes Sedai who has directed his life since Emond's Field. He strikes at Caemlyn, where the Forsaken Rahvin has been ruling Andor in disguise after enthralling its queen; when Rahvin's Power kills Aviendha, Mat, and others, Rand answers with balefire, blasting the enemy out of recent existence so completely that those deaths are undone. Mat, now a formidable battle commander with a loyal company at his back, is drawn again to Rand's side. Nynaeve and Elayne reach safety near Salidar, where rebel Aes Sedai are massing against Elaida; Nynaeve has bound the legendary heroine Birgitte into living flesh, and in the world of dreams she at last captures the Forsaken Moghedien, taking a dangerous prisoner and a store of forbidden knowledge into her keeping. Rand now commands the Aiel and much of the heartland, but he is more alone than ever, his oldest guide gone, the taint on the male Power gnawing at him, and the surviving Forsaken already plotting their next stroke.
recaps.in_short: Rand leads the Aiel out of the Waste into the nation of Cairhien, where he wars against the renegade Shaido clan, and Mat discovers a genius for command, drawing soldiers into a company of his own. When word comes that the Forsaken Rahvin has seized Andor by ensorcelling its queen, Rand strikes at Caemlyn; Rahvin's Power kills several of his friends, and Rand answers by destroying him with balefire, a fire so fierce it burns the enemy out of recent time and undoes those very deaths. Meanwhile Nynaeve and Elayne flee across the sea and travel in disguise with a traveling show toward Salidar, where Aes Sedai who reject Elaida are gathering; along the way Nynaeve pulls a legendary heroine into living flesh and, in the world of dreams, finally traps her old tormentor, the Forsaken Moghedien. And at Cairhien, the Aes Sedai Moiraine, foreseeing her own end, confronts the Forsaken Lanfear and drags her through a doorway that consumes them both, sacrificing herself and leaving Rand without the guide who has shaped his path from the start.

recaps.text: Rand al'Thor, a shepherd of the Two Rivers, was named the Dragon Reborn by the Aes Sedai Moiraine after he first channeled the One Power at the Eye of the World: the champion prophesied to fight the Dark One, and, because he wields the tainted male Power, fated to go mad. He fought the fiery-eyed Ba'alzamon in the sky above Falme, was proclaimed the Dragon before the world, and later drew the crystal sword Callandor from the Stone of Tear, killing that ancient enemy and learning it was the Forsaken Ishamael. In the fourth book Rand went to the Aiel Waste, passed through the city of Rhuidean, uncovered the buried truth of the Aiel's origins, and was accepted as their Car'a'carn, chief of chiefs, gaining a bound Forsaken as a reluctant tutor. Mat, changed by an ancient doorway, came away with a warrior's memories, a spear, and a talisman against the Power; Perrin returned to the Two Rivers, defeated a Trolloc invasion, married Faile, and was hailed as its lord; and Elayne and Nynaeve foiled a Black Ajah plot in Tanchico. In the White Tower, Elaida seized power, stilled and imprisoned the Amyrlin Siuan Sanche, and drove loyal sisters into exile, where they began to gather in the town of Salidar. As this book opens, Rand commands the Aiel and prepares to carry his war down out of the Waste, the surviving Forsaken circling him and the taint on saidin ever at work.

characters.description: Uhtred of Bebbanburg, the pagan Northumbrian warlord, now based at Dunholm in his son-in-law Sigtryggr's kingdom. Every war he has fought has been for other people's thrones; with a fragile truce holding between the Saxon kingdoms and Norse Northumbria, he means at last to fight the one that is his own - the taking of Bebbanburg, the sea fortress his family lost when he was a boy.
characters.name: Uhtred of Bebbanburg

characters.description: The Irish swordsman who has been Uhtred's closest friend and second-in-command through every campaign. If Bebbanburg is ever to be taken, Finan will be in the front of the fight.
characters.name: Finan

characters.description: Uhtred's warrior son and heir, a proven fighter with his father's stubbornness. The reclaiming of Bebbanburg is his inheritance as much as his father's obsession, and he shares every risk of the campaign.
characters.name: Uhtred (the younger)

characters.description: Uhtred's cousin, also named Uhtred, the usurping lord of Bebbanburg. Son of the uncle who stole the fortress, he has held its near-impregnable walls for years, secure behind sea, sand, and stone, and rich enough to hire swords when enemies gather.
characters.name: Uhtred (the cousin)

characters.description: King Edward's eldest son, the prince Uhtred raised and trained, whom court faction still brands illegitimate to bar him from the succession. Bold to the point of recklessness, he trusts Uhtred more than he trusts the men around his father's throne.
characters.name: Aethelstan

characters.description: The richest and most powerful ealdorman in Wessex, grandfather of Edward's second son Aelfweard, whom he means to see crowned. Ruthless behind a mask of piety, he works to destroy the rival prince Aethelstan and to extend his family's reach - and his gold moves men far beyond Wessex's borders.
characters.name: Aethelhelm

characters.description: King of Scotland, a hard and intelligent ruler with ambitions along Northumbria's northern marches. When opportunity opens in the lands around Bebbanburg, Constantin moves with an army, and he is a far more formidable enemy than any hired sword.
characters.name: Constantin

characters.description: A Norse sea-warlord whose ships and crews are for hire. Drawn into the struggle over Bebbanburg by its lord's gold, he and his men become one more wall between Uhtred and his birthright.
characters.name: Einar

characters.description: A mad Danish shipmaster who styles himself a Christian bishop, ruling his own little flock at Gyruum at the mouth of the Tyne. Half prophet, half pirate, and shrewder than his lunacy suggests, he trades in information and favors, and becomes an unlikely instrument in Uhtred's designs on Bebbanburg.
characters.name: Ieremias

recaps.ending: The book ends with the moment the whole series has pointed toward: Bebbanburg is Uhtred's. Slipping away from Aethelhelm's fleet at Grimesbi as Norsemen allied with the Scots burned it, Uhtred disguised his own ships as the supply ships the fortress was expecting, and the guards themselves opened Bebbanburg's Sea Gate to him. In the fighting that followed, the prince Aethelstan - stowed away with the help of Uhtred's son - killed Aethelhelm's champion, and Uhtred's cousin, refusing to meet him man to man, was cut down. Aethelhelm's scheme to bind the fortress to his family died with the defence, and the ealdorman himself did not survive its fall. Constantin's Scots, still in the field around the fortress they had come to take, found it held against them by its rightful lord and no longer worth the price; the siege that was meant to starve out a usurper ends with the Scots coming to terms and withdrawing. After a lifetime of fighting for other people's kingdoms, Uhtred of Bebbanburg holds his own: lord of the fortress at last, with his son as its heir - and with Aethelhelm's faction in Wessex now owing him a hatred that will outlive the old ealdorman.
recaps.in_short: With a fragile truce holding between Wessex, Mercia, and Sigtryggr's Norse Northumbria, Uhtred at last turns to his life's ambition: retaking Bebbanburg from his cousin. First he must stop a war - Ealdorman Aethelhelm has been scheming to break the truce and to have the prince Aethelstan killed under Danish colors, and Uhtred exposes the plot before the kings. Then the board shifts: Constantin of Scotland invades the Bebbanburg lands and besieges the fortress, and the trapped cousin hires Einar the White's Norse crews and looks to Aethelhelm for rescue. Uhtred threads between Scots, Norsemen, and West Saxons - using the mad bishop-pirate Ieremias, scouting Aethelhelm's fleet at Grimesbi and escaping when it burns - and finally disguises his ships as the fortress's expected supply ships. The guards open the Sea Gate themselves; Aethelstan, stowed away, kills Aethelhelm's champion; the cousin refuses single combat and dies; Aethelhelm does not survive the fall. The Scots come to terms, and Uhtred is lord of Bebbanburg at last.

recaps.text: Earlier in the series: Uhtred of Bebbanburg, a Northumbrian noble raised by Danes and still a pagan, was robbed of Bebbanburg, his family's great sea fortress, by his uncle when he was a boy; his cousin holds it now. He became the greatest warlord of the Saxon kingdoms, serving Alfred and then his children: King Edward of Wessex, and Aethelflaed, the Lady of the Mercians, whom Uhtred put on Mercia's throne. He destroyed the Danish army of Cnut Ranulfson at Teotanheale, crushed the Norse invasion of Ragnall Ivarson, and saw his old enemy Brida killed by his own daughter Stiorra - who is now queen in the north, wife of the Norse king Sigtryggr of Eoferwic, Uhtred's son-in-law, whose throne exists on a sworn promise never to attack Mercia. Uhtred raised and protects Aethelstan, King Edward's eldest son, whose claim to the succession is contested by the faction of Ealdorman Aethelhelm, grandfather of the rival prince Aelfweard. One attempt on Bebbanburg, years ago, already failed.

An uneasy truce holds between the Saxon kingdoms and Sigtryggr's Norse Northumbria, and Uhtred - based at Dunholm in his son-in-law's kingdom - wants nothing more than to spend it taking Bebbanburg back from his cousin. But the truce itself is under quiet attack. West Saxon troops have planted themselves in a fort on Northumbrian soil, churchmen are preaching holy war, and behind the provocations Uhtred begins to trace the hand of Ealdorman Aethelhelm, the most powerful man in Wessex, who profits from a war however it ends. Sigtryggr looks to his father-in-law to keep the peace his throne depends on, while Uhtred's own plans for his fortress must wait on the politics he despises. Along the way Uhtred deals with one of the stranger powers of the Northumbrian coast: Ieremias, the mad Danish shipmaster who calls himself a bishop and rules his own flock at the mouth of the Tyne, a man whose madness hides a sharp instinct for profit and information.

Uhtred unpicks Aethelhelm's scheme: the provocations on the border were bait for a manufactured atrocity - West Saxons killed under Danish colors so that outrage would force Edward into war with Northumbria, with the prince Aethelstan conveniently among the dead and the blame on Sigtryggr. Uhtred foils the ambush and then confronts the plot openly before the assembled powers, exposing the scheme where Edward, Aethelflaed, and Sigtryggr can all hear it; the truce holds and Aethelhelm's design collapses, though the ealdorman himself remains untouchable. Then the north upends Uhtred's plans entirely: Constantin of Scotland marches an army into the Bebbanburg lands and lays siege to the fortress itself. Uhtred's cousin, penned behind his walls, hires the Norse sea-warlord Einar the White and looks south for allies - and Aethelhelm, seeing a chance to gain a foothold and a marriage bond with the fortress, prepares a fleet. Bebbanburg, which Uhtred meant to pry from one enemy, is now the prize in a race between Scots, Norse hirelings, West Saxon gold, and Uhtred's own small band. His path takes him to Grimesbi among Aethelhelm's gathering ships, where he scouts the enemy fleet and slips away undetected when Norsemen allied with the Scots burn it in the night.

Uhtred takes Bebbanburg. With the Scots blockading the land approaches and the garrison waiting on Aethelhelm's help, Uhtred plays the one card no wall can stop: expectation. His ships, disguised as the supply ships the fortress is desperate for, are welcomed in, and the guards open the Sea Gate to their own destruction. In the savage fight inside the walls, the prince Aethelstan - who stowed away with the connivance of Uhtred's son - kills Aethelhelm's champion, and Uhtred's cousin, offered single combat and refusing it, is killed. Aethelhelm's hopes of binding the fortress to his family die in the same fight, and the old ealdorman does not survive Bebbanburg's fall - a death his son will lay at Uhtred's feet for years to come. Constantin's Scots, who came to starve out a usurper, find the fortress held by its rightful lord and no cheap victory left; they come to terms and withdraw. The book ends with the series' oldest promise kept: Uhtred, who was robbed of Bebbanburg as a boy and fought a lifetime for other men's thrones, stands lord of his own fortress, his son beside him as its heir.

characters.description: The eldest of the three children at the cottage by the Enchanted Wood. Well used to the Faraway Tree by now, Joe helps show a difficult new house-guest the ropes and keeps a level head when the lands above the tree turn tricky.
characters.name: Joe

characters.description: One of the two sisters, warm and sensible, who welcomes the visiting girl even when her airs make her hard to like. She shares the climbs up the tree and the adventures in its changing lands.
characters.name: Beth

characters.description: The youngest of the three children, quick to enjoy the magic of the tree and just as quick to lose patience with a boastful guest. She joins every visit to the folk of the trunk and the lands at the top.
characters.name: Frannie

characters.description: A girl who comes to stay with the children - prim, sure she is always right, and scornful of any talk about a magic tree. Her conceit makes her an awkward guest at first, but the tree folk and the strange lands above steadily take her down a peg, and by the end she is a good deal humbler and kinder.
characters.name: Connie

characters.description: The golden-haired elf of the Faraway Tree, gentle and helpful as ever. She greets the children and their sceptical guest, offers her treats, and keeps an eye on which land is currently sitting at the top of the tree.
characters.name: Silky

characters.description: The good-natured wanderer hung with clattering saucepans and kettles, whose poor hearing turns plain remarks into comic muddles. He remains a staunch friend of the children on their journeys up and above the tree.
characters.name: the Saucepan Man

characters.description: The round-faced little fellow near the top of the Faraway Tree, keeper of the slippery-slip that whirls riders down the trunk on a cushion. He hosts the children and their guest to tea and helps steer them through the tree's ever-changing lands.
characters.name: Moon-Face

characters.description: The stern mistress of a strict school in one of the lands that visits the top of the tree. She deals out slaps to any pupil she judges naughty, and the children fall into her clutches when the land above turns out to be hers; getting free of her school is one of the book's tighter escapes.
characters.name: Dame Slap

recaps.ending: The book, and the series, ends with Connie fully reformed. Near the close she loses her voice as a punishment for eavesdropping in the Land of Secrets, and it is given back to her only in the Land of Enchantments, a place dangerous enough that several of the group are nearly lost there for good before all are brought out safely. When the Faraway Tree seems to wither and die, its folk band together to save it. Humbled by her adventures, Connie has shed her boastful manner and become genuinely fond of the tree and its people. The friends celebrate with a final visit to a Land of Treats, full of ice creams, a roundabout ridden on live animals, balloon rides and a circus. Connie is sad that her stay is over, and the children say a fond good-bye to Moon-Face, Silky, the Saucepan Man and the rest, and to the Faraway Tree itself. As the last of the three books, it leaves no thread open: the door on the Enchanted Wood is closed with the tree safe and its folk secure.
recaps.in_short: A stuck-up, disbelieving girl named Connie comes to stay with the children while her mother is unwell, and scoffs at the idea of a magic tree - until the folk of the Faraway Tree, from the ink-throwing Angry Pixie to Dame Washalot's wash-water, show her otherwise. Climbing to the lands at the top, the group visit a Land of Giants, a Nursery Rhyme Land and the school of the strict Dame Slap, and have to search for Connie when she vanishes in the Land of Marvels. Later Connie loses her voice for eavesdropping in the Land of Secrets and has it restored only in the perilous Land of Enchantments, where several of the friends are nearly lost. When the Faraway Tree itself begins to wither, its folk work together to save it. By the end Connie has been humbled and grown fond of the tree, and after a last visit to a Land of Treats the children bid the tree and its folk a fond farewell, closing the series.

recaps.text: Across the first two books, a brother and his two sisters found the Enchanted Wood and the great Faraway Tree that rises through the clouds, its top opening by a ladder onto lands that change from time to time. They befriended the folk of the trunk - Moon-Face and his slippery-slip, the golden-haired elf Silky, the half-deaf Saucepan Man, the peevish Angry Pixie, the sleepy Mister Watzisname and Dame Washalot with her cascading wash-water - and learned that each land could be a treat or a trap and had to be left before it moved on. In the second book a cousin came to stay and was won over to the tree, and when the children's mother fell ill they fetched a cure from the Land of Magic Medicines. Every visit follows the same pattern: climb the tree, go up into whatever land is resting there, and come safely down again before it swings away.

A girl named Connie comes to stay with the children while her own mother is unwell and away for a long rest. Connie is bossy and pleased with herself, and she flatly refuses to believe there is anything magic about the wood or the tree. The children take her in among the folk of the Faraway Tree, where her airs get short shrift: the Angry Pixie flings ink at her through his window and Dame Washalot's wash-water catches her on the way up. The children introduce her to Moon-Face and the others, and tea with Moon-Face begins to shake her disbelief. Around this time the Saucepan Man's mother gives up her place as a baker in Dame Slap's land and comes to live in the tree, where she opens a shop selling cakes and sweets. For all that she has seen, Connie's superior manner still needs a good deal of softening.

As the group climb to the lands at the top of the tree, Connie's boastful ways keep landing her in difficulty, and the tree and its folk refuse to be impressed by her. They visit a Land of Giants, reached by way of a beanstalk, and a Nursery Rhyme Land where figures such as Jack and Jill and little Miss Muffet are met in person. A visit to the land of the strict schoolmistress Dame Slap goes wrong and most of the party are shut up in her school, so that the two sisters have to contrive a rescue. In the Land of Marvels Connie wanders off and vanishes, and the others have an anxious search before she is found and brought safely back. Through these scrapes Connie slowly begins to lose her airs and to see the worth of her new friends.

Toward the end the friends face their sharpest dangers. In the Land of Secrets, Connie listens in on a secret that is not hers to hear, and as a punishment her voice is taken away. It can be restored only in the Land of Enchantments, which comes to the tree next, and that land proves so dangerous that several of the group are nearly lost in it for good before all are brought safely out and Connie can speak again. At one point the Faraway Tree itself seems to wither and sicken, and it is the folk of the tree, working together, who save it. By now Connie has changed completely: her boastfulness is gone and she has grown truly fond of the tree and its people. The friends round off their adventures with a visit to a Land of Treats - ice creams, a roundabout ridden on live animals, balloon rides and a circus. Connie is sorry to leave, and the children say a fond good-bye to the Faraway Tree and its folk, closing the series.

characters.description: Captain of the Tennyson, a human vessel operating under Ornu rule. He quietly coordinates with Bina Chakravarti beyond Imperial surveillance while deciding how to investigate an ancient transmission without exposing his crew to punishment.
characters.name: Bill Henderson

characters.description: The Tennyson's experienced executive officer and Bill Henderson's long-serving second-in-command. She helps trace the unexplained signal and uses a subtle sign language with Bill to communicate beyond Imperial surveillance.
characters.name: Bina Chakravarti

characters.description: The Tennyson's communications officer, who detects a scrambled transmission that repeats aboard the ship.
characters.name: Sally Longfield

characters.description: A Marine serving with Alden Stone's team aboard the Tennyson.
characters.name: Funnybone

characters.description: A hostile Ornu official who observes the Tennyson's human crew on behalf of the Imperium.
characters.name: The Tennyson's Ornu monitor

characters.description: Captain of the Tennyson's seven-person Marine team. He monitors a discouraged crew, tries to prevent unrest, and joins the ancient-signal investigation while Imperial kill switches constrain the command staff.
characters.name: Alden Stone

characters.description: An Ornu consul on Earth and the uncle of the Tennyson's monitor. His authority gives his nephew influence over the investigation into the ancient transmission.
characters.name: Philo

characters.description: A new Marine private on Stone's team, also known as Newby. She has already witnessed the Imperium impose summary punishment on her former captain.
characters.name: Jen Lambert

characters.description: The newest Marine on Stone's team. He is literal-minded and inexperienced, and joins the team's assignment to monitor crew morale.
characters.name: Porker

characters.description: A Marine serving with Alden Stone's team aboard the Tennyson.
characters.name: Splat

characters.description: A member of Stone's Marine team assigned to watch crew morale as the ancient signal draws the Tennyson into danger.
characters.name: Termite

characters.description: The Tennyson's weapons officer, involved as the crew traces the ancient transmission to an object near an asteroid.
characters.name: Hans Norder
